items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Ben and I were like brothers because his grandmother used to have a restaurant in Kansas City and she used to feed Ben and I, you know. And we were always hanging out together and running around together then.

ctx.x: Well, the Moten band, they seemed to have a lot of jazz players in there?
Yeah, but in the Moten band the only guys that went out at night and played was Ben WEBSTER and

myself and possibly Eddie Durham. But the rest of the guys just would come in -- and lips (PHONETIC). But a lot of the guys would come out and listen, see. And guys went around looking for each other, you know. This is where we picked up our ideas. You take when Coleman Hawkins was living, every-time a new tenor player would come around that anybody was talking about, Coleman Hawkins would be there listening to him at night, see.
